INTRODUCTION

Your code. Its memory. Its rules.

AFWE keeps track of what your codebase is supposed to be, what it actually is, and the rules that keep it together: so AI agents can work with real context, not guesswork.

GET STARTED IN 1 MINUTE Rust CLI
$ cargo install afwe
$ afwe onboard --profile engineer

The big picture

AI coding agents rarely lose track of your code. They lose track of why it is the way it is.

Ask two agents for a narrow-body engine of 27,000 to 35,000 lbf and you get two good, different designs. One is a two-spool engine that is cheap to maintain. The other is a three-spool engine that burns less fuel and costs more to service. Neither is wrong. Fifteen prompts later, a third agent sees code that works, cannot tell which trade-off you chose on purpose, and refactors it.

That is the source of silent collateral damage: in turn 1 an agent builds a billing integration; in turn 15 an agent refactors a UI component and breaks the billing contract. A feature disappears and nobody declared it.

Why it exists

Line drift and context windows make this worse, but the fundamental problem is that your intent was never recorded next to the code. Vendor-side memory does not solve this: it lives inside a proprietary cloud product, not in your git history, so the next agent or teammate never receives it.

AFWE introduces double-entry bookkeeping for autonomous coding: your repository records not only the source files, but also their living architecture, constraints, locked human decisions (pins), and audit receipts.

A different approach

AFWE is built on four core principles:

  • The folder is the product: All architectural knowledge lives in human-readable YAML and Markdown inside .afwe/ in your repository.
  • Deterministic verification: AFWE never makes internal model calls. Decisions are 100% reproducible using Rust Tree-Sitter AST parsers, BLAKE3 content hashing, and reproducible pre-commit checks.
  • Pre-code claims: Agents must declare their intents and structural claims before modifying source files. If a claim violates a locked Pin, AFWE triggers REDO before any code is generated.
  • Continuous architectural feedback: Knowledge graphs, intent memory, and pre-commit tripwires form a single loop that gates every change.

1. The First Screen (Overview)

Running afwe status or opening the AFWE Studio gives you an immediate health dashboard: total mapped nodes, active pins, unresolved proposals, and architectural drift. If an agent creates a file without attaching it to an architectural node, AFWE surfaces it immediately.

2. The Codebase Blueprint

The Blueprint translates complex directory trees into an interactive architectural sunburst. You can drill down into components, view active boundary constraints, inspect recent turn receipts, and verify allowed dependency relationships.

Who it's for

Engineers using AI agents

Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or OpenCode who need agents to respect invariants without manual babysitting.

Founders and tech leads

Teams moving rapidly with autonomous coding where architectural coherence must be preserved across weeks and months.

Key benefits

ZERO DRIFT

Deterministic Gates

Changes that violate constraints or block pins are rejected before hitting git.

RECOVERY

3-Way Restoration

Recover deleted features from earlier turns using automated 3-way merge.

OPEN CORE

100% Free MIT

No feature paywalls, no mandatory cloud accounts, and zero tracking.
